changes.title: Amazon EC2 launches performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring
changes.detail: Customers can now use Amazon EC2 performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring to observe and act on the performance of their EC2 workloads without setup within the instance, complementing their in-guest tooling. Customers running performance-sensitive EC2 workloads can use these signals to monitor their CPU and GPU resources, tune capacity needs, and troubleshoot application issues. changes.title: AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust is now generally available
changes.detail: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the open source AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust. Rust developers can use the SDK to build resilient, long-running workflows using Lambda durable functions, to create multi-step applications like infrastructure automation, deployment rollouts with approval gates, and pipelines that call AI models and pause for human review directly in their Rust code without implementing custom progress tracking. changes.title: AgentCore runtime instances now support privileged mode
changes.detail: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support privileged mode, which lets your agents install system-level software and run nested containers. Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. You turn on privileged mode when you create or update an agent runtime that runs on runtime instances. For example, a coding agent can start its service dependencies, such as Postgres and Redis, as containers and run its integration tests against them.
